adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Indonesia - Wikipedia
adds.summary: English Wikipedia, 'LGBTQ rights in Indonesia' (article at the Transgender rights in Indonesia redirect; page last edited 4 Oct 2026): national-framework record of how LGBTQ and transgender people fare in Indonesian custody. Verified content: police raids and mass arrests of LGBTQ people under pornography/morality law (e.g. 141 men arrested at a Jakarta 'gay sex party', May 2017); source [86] cited that 'gays in jails are often sexually abused due to their sexual orientation' and often do not report it out of fear of being sent back to prison; transgender women in Aceh were arrested in January 2018, had their heads shaved, and were forced into men's clothing, with some stripped and paraded; in Jakarta the Social Agency 'regularly conducted raids against transgender women' and detained trans people are incarcerated in city-owned 'rehabilitation' centres alongside homeless people, beggars and street buskers, released only on signature of a statement. The article records no statutory rule placing trans prisoners by gender identity; placement and conditions follow Indonesia's ordinary detention practice.

records.note: No North Sumatra-specific record of where trans prisoners are housed was found: the province-targeted Wikipedia full-text search returned zero hits, and the only additional candidate fetched (a BBC feature on Indonesian trans people, news/world-asia-40602298) returned no usable article content. The verified national framework applies to North Sumatra as to every Indonesian province: transgender detainees are processed through ordinary detention (police custody and prisons) with no gender-identity-based placement rule, while the framework's documented enforcement hotspots (Jakarta raids and 'rehabilitation'-centre incarceration of waria; the January 2018 Aceh arrests and forced re-clothing of trans women) sit in other provinces. For a trans visitor or resident in North Sumatra, the prison-housing question is undocumented at province level; the national pattern of police arrests under morality laws plus abuse of LGBTQ people in jails is the standing risk structure.

records.note: No North Sulawesi-specific record of where trans prisoners are housed was found: the province-targeted Wikipedia full-text search returned zero hits, and both candidate fetches came back thin for this topic — the English Wikipedia biography of Merlyn Sopjan (the best-known trans activist associated with the archipelago, page fetched this run) contains no prison, detention or police content and documents her career in Malang (East Java), while the 'Waria' article resolves to a one-line disambiguation page. The verified national framework applies to North Sulawesi too: transgender detainees go through ordinary Indonesian detention with no gender-identity-based placement rule, and the documented abuse pattern (sexual abuse of LGBTQ people in jails; Jakarta 'rehabilitation'-centre incarceration of detained waria; the January 2018 Aceh arrests) is recorded in other provinces, leaving any North Sulawesi trans-prisoner housing practice undocumented.
